annotation.title_clean: К ВОПРОСУ О РЕГЛАМЕНТАЦИИ И СОДЕРЖАНИИ СИСТЕМЫ ПРАВОВЫХ ПРИНЦИПОВ ВЗАИМОДЕЙСТВИЯ ЧЕЛОВЕКА С ИСКУССТВЕННЫМ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТОМ, РОБОТАМИ И ОБЪЕКТАМИ РОБОТОТЕХНИКИ
annotation.title_en: On the Regulation and Content of a System of Legal Principles for Human Interaction with Artificial Intelligence, Robots and Objects of Robotics
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Russian legal journal article using comparative and doctrinal analysis to identify legal principles for human interaction with AI, robots and robotics objects. It criticizes Russia's Moscow AI experiment law No. 123-FZ for lacking such principles and proposes humanism, non-discrimination, dignity, confidentiality, disclosure, presumption of innocence and informed consent.
key_provisions_or_claims: Humanism (anthropocentrism) should be the foundational principle of AI and robotics regulation.
Moscow AI experiment law No. 123-FZ lacks principles on human-AI interaction and liability for AI errors.
Proposed principles: justice, non-discrimination, no harm, dignity, confidentiality, disclosure, autonomy of will, informed consent.
Presumption of innocence needed against AI decisions, e.g., Moscow COVID social monitoring app.
Calls for systematic new legislation rather than piecemeal amendments.
